articles.title: Oil prices drop by 2% as US considers easing Russian tanker sanctions
articles.description: Oil prices declined by about 2% on Thursday, 15 October, following reports that the US is considering measures to relax restrictions on tankers associated with Russia's so-called “shadow fleet”.

articles.title: JERA acquires JOGMEC’s shares in Wheatstone LNG project vehicle
articles.description: Japanese energy company JERA has completed the purchase of all shares held by the Japan Organization for Metals and Energy Security (JOGMEC) in Pan Pacific Energy (PEJ), the entity it uses to invest in Australia's Wheatstone LNG Project.

articles.title: North Sea Production Emissions Fall for 6th Straight Year
articles.description: The North Sea Transition Authority announced that emissions in the North Sea have fallen for a sixth consecutive year.

articles.title: Container Ship Sinks in Strait of Hormuz
articles.description: All 21 crew members were evacuated without injuries before the Singapore-flagged vessel sank.

articles.title: Monumental Energy joins consortium to drill Maata prospect in Taranaki, NZ
articles.description: Canada-listed explorer Monumental Energy has announced plans to take an ownership interest in the Maata oil field through a consortium of four companies operating in New Zealand's onshore Taranaki Basin.

articles.title: Ship-to-Ship Oil Transfers Surge Off India’s West Coast
articles.description: The waters outside the Strait of Hormuz have been so overcrowded with ship-to-ship transfers to keep oil flowing out of the Persian Gulf that the STS operations are expanding into India’s West Coast. A total of 82 cargoes, or about 680,000 barrels per day (bpd), were transferred onto larger ships in the Indian Gulf of Kutch in September, according to vessel-tracking data by Vortexa cited by The National. The Gulf of Kutch, which opens towards the Arabian Sea facing the Gulf of Oman, has become another point of STS for the Gulf oil producers.…

articles.title: India’s Annual Wind Power Installations to Double by 2030
articles.description: India’s record-setting annual additions of wind power capacity could double by the end of the decade, a senior executive at major wind turbine maker Suzlon Energy told Bloomberg on Thursday. Last year, India installed a record 6.3 gigawatts (GW) of wind power generation capacity. This year, the annual installations are set to top that record and reach 8 GW, and annual additions could then double to about 14 GW by 2030, Suzlon Energy’s executive vice chairman, Girish Tanti, told Bloomberg TV on the sidelines of the Bloomberg New Economy…

articles.title: TotalEnergies Eyes Massive Profit Windfall as Refining Margins Soar
articles.description: TotalEnergies expects to report strong third-quarter results later this month as the Middle East conflict has driven up refining margins and LNG prices in a bull market, the French oil and gas supermajor said on Thursday. TotalEnergies said in a trading update its European refining margin soared to as much as $33.20 per barrel in the third quarter, nearly tripled from $13.50 for the second quarter, and quadrupled from the $8.40 refining margin in the third quarter last year. “Downstream results and cash flow are expected to reach exceptional…

articles.title: Ukraine to Resume Russian Oil Refinery Strikes After Failed Energy Ceasefire
articles.description: Ukraine will resume drone strikes on Russian refineries after Russia kept hitting energy infrastructure and killing civilians in Ukraine despite U.S. President Trump’s claim of an “energy ceasefire”, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told the Financial Times. In the interview in London, the Ukrainian President told FT he had ordered a pause in strikes on Russian refineries for three days to comply with the U.S. wishes. Meanwhile, Russia continued to strike Ukraine’s energy infrastructure and kill civilians, Zelenskyy…

articles.title: IMF Warns of Worldwide Fallout as Attacks on Saudi Arabia Escalate
articles.description: Strikes on Saudi infrastructure by the Yemeni Houthis could affect the global economy, the managing director of the International Monetary Fund has warned. Speaking at a joint event with the World Bank in Thailand, Kristalina Georgieva said that despite this danger, Saudi Arabia remains resilient and has a better economic outlook than most of its neighbors thanks to its diversification efforts in recent years as it aimed to reduce the share of oil revenues in its budget. Still, the situation remains difficult, with a high risk of further rises…

articles.title: Lithium Prices Plunge as EU-China Trade Deal Sparks Demand Fears
articles.description: Lithium prices have slumped, following a deal between the European Union and China that will cut Chinese hybrid car exports to the bloc. Since the start of the week, China’s most actively traded lithium futures contract has dropped by 14%, Bloomberg reported earlier today. The oil crisis caused by the war in the Middle East had sparked hopes that battery demand will expand, as drivers increasingly switch from gasoline and diesel cars to electric vehicles. However, protectionist measures taken by European Union authorities against Chinese…

articles.title: Oil Prices Fall as Trump Considers Easing Sanctions on Shadow Fleet Tankers
articles.description: Crude oil prices retreated from yesterday’s highs earlier today, on the news that President Trump was considering lifting sanctions on tankers used to transport oil and fuels from Venezuela, Russia, and Iran in a bid to ease a deepening tanker crunch. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $104.39 per barrel, after earlier in the week it topped $106, while West Texas Intermediate was trading at $94.02 per barrel, after yesterday it climbed close to $96 per barrel. The war in the Persian Gulf has tightened the availability of tankers…

articles.title: Aramco's New China Refinery Venture Gets 1st Crude Cargo
articles.description: Saudi Aramco and its local partners have received the first crude cargo for their new refining complex in China.

articles.title: Oil Gains as Global Supply Risks Mount
articles.description: Oil gained amid renewed supply disruptions, rising shipping costs and continued pressure on global fuel markets.

articles.title: Brookfield, NextEra to Build $100 Billion AI Hub on Cold War Nuclear Site
articles.description: The U.S. Department of Energy (DoE) has announced a landmark $100-billion private investment to turn the former uranium enrichment site in Western Kentucky into the new Paducah American Energy Hub, marking one of the largest economic development projects in Kentucky's history. Led by U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright, the initiative will bring together a private-sector coalition to build a massive artificial intelligence and high-performance computing (HPC) innovation campus powered by new energy infrastructure. The phased buildout is targeted…

articles.title: Oil Market Tightens as Tanker Attacks and Inventory Draws Mount
articles.description: Brent crude is once again over $106, Iran is intensifying attacks on tankers in Hormuz, and global inventories are draining, while OPEC just forecast stronger demand for next year. Six months ago, one well-timed TruthSocial post by President Trump would have calmed traders down. Now, this no longer works as fundamentals trump talk. Earlier in the war between the United States and Israel, and Iran, U.S. top officials could push prices lower with a statement about peace talks. There was even a brief ceasefire in June that pressured prices for weeks,…

articles.title: White House Turns to Korean War-Era Law as Diesel Prices Stay Above $6
articles.description: The United States has used a 1950 authority to help boost fuel production at a small Texas refinery, Vice President JD Vance said on Tuesday, as the Trump Administration is running out of levers to lower record-high fuel prices. “I am pleased to announce that the Trump administration, working with the refinery at Delek, has used the Defense Production Act and we’re going to expand the refinery right here in Tyler, Texas,” Vance said at a political rally in Texas. “We want millions of gallons of commercial-grade and military-spec…

articles.title: US Crude Oil Inventories See Massive Drop Off
articles.description: The American Petroleum Institute (API) estimated that crude oil inventories in the United States fell by a massive 11.12 million barrels in the week ending October 9. In the week prior, US crude oil inventories fell by 2.09 million barrels. Commercial crude oil inventories excluding the SPR have lost more than 51 million barrels over the last 26 weeks, but US crude inventories are at roughly the same level as they were at the beginning of the year, according to API data, kept in check in part thanks to draws from the SPR. For the week ending October…

articles.title: Trump Announces $80 Billion Taiwan LNG Deal
articles.description: President Donald Trump has announced a massive new energy agreement with Taiwan, claiming the island will purchase between $70 billion and $80 billion worth of liquefied natural gas from Alaska over the next two decades, as Asian importers scramble to secure supplies beyond the increasingly dangerous Strait of Hormuz. In a Truth Social post on Wednesday, Trump said Taiwan had committed to purchasing 30% of the planned Alaska LNG project's output for 20 years, alongside a $4.4 billion equity investment. articles.description: The Strait of Hormuz's closure has reduced LNG supply; GlobalData analysis identifies how export routes have changed.
